transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Lopez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ethan Walker (Cedar - Head of ML), Sara Bennett (Cedar - Cloud Infra), Liam O'Connor (Cedar - CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick renewal check-in; customer wants expansion to EU region and a 20% increase in reserved capacity for Q3; discuss pricing and compliance.

[00:00] Maya Lopez: Alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Ethan Walker: Ethan here.
[00:10] Sara Bennett: Sara here.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Liam on.
[00:14] Maya Lopez: Great, Maya and Priya from Redwood. Goal today is renewal + expansion options, sizing, and next steps.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Yeah quick context from our side — last quarter you were using a mix of hosted and a small dedicated pool. You mentioned latency issues for EU customers and some surge nights, is that still the case?
[00:45] Ethan Walker: Yeah still seeing spikes. The EU traffic has grown faster than we forecasted. Right now we hit a few high p90 latencies during billing windows. Not a ton but it's visible and our product folks are asking for regional presence.
[01:05] Sara Bennett: Also the infra team wants to move more traffic into our VPC for compliance reasons, TTLs and request tracing, and they want KMS integration.
[01:20] Priya Shah: Totally makes sense. For region expansion we can provision dedicated capacity in eu-west1 under Redwood Dedicated, and we have private VPC options for the dedicated pools. KMS/HSM is supported, and we can provide audit logs for queries — though note we redact by default for hosted but dedicated/private gives more control.
[01:45] Liam O'Connor: On the commercial side, we're looking at a contract extension through next year if the numbers make sense. What sort of discount tiers do you offer for committed spend increases?
[01:58] Maya Lopez: Good question. We typically tier discounts by committed GPU-months and contract length. For a 12-month extension with a 20-30% capacity increase we can propose a blended unit discount and waive part of the setup for an additional region. I'll put exact numbers in the proposal.
[02:16] Ethan Walker: Can you also show cost scenarios for burst vs reserved-only? We have unpredictable spikes so burst is important.
[02:25] Priya Shah: Yep. Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and configurable autoscale policies. The economics differ — bursts are pay-as-you-go at a premium but avoid overcommit; reserved is cheaper per-token but needs correct sizing. We'll include sample TCO scenarios.
[02:45] Sara Bennett: A few technical checks: do you support peering into our VPC or will it be a private link? We prefer peering for egress control.
[02:55] Priya Shah: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on cloud provider. For peering there are IP allowlist considerations and we'll share the runbook. There might be minor routing steps for prefix advertisement but nothing unusual.
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: SOC 2 status? Our audit team will want that on file.
[03:16] Maya Lopez: We're SOC 2 Type II certified — happy to share the report under NDA. We also have ISO docs and a KMS integration playbook.
[03:25] Ethan Walker: Perf: can we run a short benchmark in our VPC to validate latency and p95 on the dedicated pool? Maybe 2 hours with representative load.
[03:33] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We'll need test creds and a small syn load script; Priya to send runbook, we'll run it with the proposed capacity profile. Expect to see reduced p95 if you move east-west traffic into region.
[03:50] Sara Bennett: One heads up — legal might ask for data residency guarantees for EU users. We need region pinning.
[03:58] Maya Lopez: We can pin model serving to eu-west1 and route EU traffic there; we'll include routing policy details. For strict residency we'll note logs and backups are also regionally scoped on Private.
[04:15] Ethan Walker: Are there any limitations on quantized models or specific kernels on the dedicated pool? Some of our workloads use 8-bit quantization.
[04:24] Priya Shah: No major limits — our runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths. We'll validate the exact model variant during onboarding; occasionally some custom ops need a fallback but we handle that in the rollout plan.
[04:40] Maya Lopez: Quick commercial recap: we'll send a renewal proposal with a 12-month term, scenarios for +20% reserved capacity and burst buffers, and pricing for adding eu-west1 and optional ap-southeast1.
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: If we sign on for 12 months and two regions, what's the lead time to stand up dedicated capacity?
[05:03] Priya Shah: Typically 2-4 weeks for dedicated pools including network setup; VPC peering can add a few days depending on approvals. We'll include a timeline in the proposal.
[05:18] Ethan Walker: Fine. Also curious about SLAs — latency SLOs or just uptime?
[05:23] Priya Shah: Our SLA is uptime-focused for Dedicated with latency SLO guidance per model and instance type in the runbook. For strict latency guarantees we can propose higher-tier SLAs at the enterprise level.
[05:40] Sara Bennett: Ok next steps?
[05:43] Maya Lopez: Action items: I'll send the pricing and region add proposal by Monday (2026-03-29). Priya will send the benchmark runbook and we can schedule the 2-hour test the week of 2026-04-06. Sara will confirm VPC peering details by 2026-04-05.
[06:05] Ethan Walker: Sounds good. One more ask — can you include a comparison vs GigaAI and CloudVendorX in the deck? Our procurement wants competitive context.
[06:15] Maya Lopez: Sure, we can include a short competitor matrix focused on latency, region coverage, and support model.
[06:22] Liam O'Connor: Great, thanks everyone.
[06:25] Maya Lopez: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the proposal and runbook.

Auto Action Items (end of transcript): Maya to send pricing/proposal; Priya send runbook; Sara confirm network details.
